chapter: Las Vegas, Sinatra and later years
title: Never unhappy playing in fifty years; always changing groups
summary: Playing since 1925 he never went back to a group or format he'd done, never typed as a leader, ending with a last quintet.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Ah -- when -- wait one second now, yeah. We're getting philosophic now --
Well what did you say -- you've never been unhappy playing --
Well, let's see. I started in 1925, it's over 50 years.

But I've never been unhappy playing and I've never gone back to something I didn't enjoy going. IN other words, from group to group, I never went back and did a lot of things, in other words, I'd keep going to different things.
-- to the trio to the quintet or the sextet on 52nd Street -- to the group with Shorty Rogers.
You didn't have to go back and repeat yourself.
You just could always break ground.
No. In other words I was never typed in any one position --
Like a lot of band leaders are.
And even with the quintet, I had different quintets.
Like the last one I had, oh it was -- it was Sam Most, and Gene Cherico, who works with Sinatra now and who else did I have on drums? Oh, I had J. C. Heard.
J. C. Heard, ah -- Sam Moss, Jimmy Wible, the same guitar player, and myself, that's the five of us, it was a great group. Wonderful group.
